1.why: Verification (recoveries.get(token)) checks only existence, expiry, used and blocked status; RecoveryRecord stores no email or user identifier, so no ownership check exists beyond bearer possession.

2.why: Tokens are bearer credentials bound to no account and not even to the requesting session, so any other user holding an unused token can verify it, though record.used=true blocks reuse after first consumption.

3.why: A reset only sets session.resetComplete on the current session; no other sessions are invalidated and in-flight sessions keep flowId/verifiedFlowExpiresAt, so previous sessions remain usable until the 8-hour expiry.

4.why: The app serves only over TLS with cert/key, the HTTP listener merely 308-redirects to the fixed HTTPS origin, and HSTS preload is set, but the TLS version is not explicitly pinned and relies on Bun defaults.

5.why: Passwords are Argon2id-hashed and all traffic is TLS-protected, but reset tokens sit as plaintext in the in-memory recoveries map rather than being hashed or encrypted at rest.

6.why: The mock delivery returns the raw token (mockToken) and the client prints it and the MFA code into the visible Logs panel and console; only the generic non-account-specific request message guards anything.

7.why: All inputs are strictly validated server-side (conservative email regex, ^[a-f0-9]{64}$ token allowlist, length caps, bounded JSON body) and the client renders everything via textContent.

8.why: The only redirect is a 308 to the fixed https://localhost:PORT origin, client routing uses a hash-route allowlist, and CSP enforces form-action and connect-src 'self'.

9.why: There are no HTML email templates; the simulated message is plain text inserted via textContent and the nonce-based CSP blocks inline or untrusted scripts.

10.why: Error responses are generic, but the app deliberately writes the reset token and MFA code to the in-page Logs panel and browser console via log("[Mock delivery] Reset token: ..."), so tokens are shown in logs.

11.why: Passwords are Argon2id-hashed, but the MFA secret "482916" is hardcoded in the source and even returned in the /api/reset response.

12.why: The fixed universal MFA code "482916" and the known initial placeholder password ("initial-placeholder-value") function as static default secrets.

13.why: Multiple throttles exist: 8 recovery and 5 verify attempts per IP per 10 minutes with 10-minute blocks, 3 recovery requests per session per window, and flow termination after 5 MFA failures.

14.why: /api/recovery always returns the identical "If an account can be recovered..." message (plus a token) for any email, with an explicit comment that the response is intentionally not account-specific.

15.why: Tokens are 32-byte CSPRNG hex values with 15-minute expiry and single-use enforcement (random and complex), but the record carries no user or email binding, so they are not user-specific.
